meta.aciklama: AI just upgraded another AI without training it. MIT researchers gave GPT-6 Astra the raw weights of Qwen 3.5, a tiny 0.8-billion-parameter model small enough to run on your own device, and asked it to make it better at math. Astra found what was causing the model to get stuck in reasoning loops and edited just 0.016% of its weights. Math scores jumped from 7.9% to 48.1%, and instruction following tripled, with no training at all. Could big AI soon tune your local AI for you? transkript.t: It's insane, an MIT student just figured out how to use models like Claude and OpenAI to
train local models to make them better.
The student's name is Rikia, and what he did is use ChatGBT6 Astra to fine-tune one
of Quinn's smallest models for math.
It gives us a lot of optimism to use models like Opus 5.5 and Vable 5.5 and as well
as Astra to make better local models for ourselves.
The whole process was pretty strenuous, obviously Carpathian others have had research
in the Serena, but nobody was able to crack it.
Students' work could be the beginning for us to own our own intelligence.
This goes without saying, the providers will always have the stronger models, but we might
not need that for our daily life.
This might be really the beginning of the local intelligence age.
